statement: A quadratic form over a field K is a map q : V → K from a finite-dimensional K-vector space V to K such that q(av) = a^2 q(v) for all a ∈ K, v ∈ V and the function (u, v) ↦ q(u + v) − q(u) − q(v) is a bilinear form; concretely, an n-ary quadratic form in n variables is a homogeneous polynomial of degree 2 given by q(x_1, ..., x_n) = ∑_{i=1}^n ∑_{j=1}^n a_{ij} x_i x_j = x^T A x, where A = (a_{ij}) is an n × n matrix over K and x is an n × 1 column vector.

symbols.meaning: finite-dimensional vector space over field K
matrix of coefficients determining the quadratic form

properties.property: Unique symmetric matrix representation: Over a field of characteristic different from 2, every quadratic form q_A(x) = x^T A x is uniquely determined by the symmetric matrix B = (1/2)(A + A^T), so that q_A(x) = x^T B x.
properties.why: Cross-terms depend only on the sums a_{ij} + a_{ji}, establishing a one-to-one correspondence between quadratic forms and symmetric matrices when 2 is invertible.

properties.property: Change of basis and congruence: Under an invertible linear change of variables x = C y with C ∈ GL(n, K), the quadratic form transforms with matrix B = C^T A C.
properties.why: Substituting the coordinate transformation C into x^T A x yields (Cy)^T A (Cy) = y^T (C^T A C) y.

properties.property: Equivalence to diagonal form: Every quadratic form in n variables over a field of characteristic not equal to 2 is equivalent to a diagonal form q(x) = ∑_{i=1}^n a_i x_i^2.
properties.why: Orthogonal or invertible linear transformations diagonalize the representing symmetric matrix.

properties.property: Polarization and correspondence with symmetric bilinear forms: When the characteristic of K is not 2, the associated bilinear form b_q(x, y) = (1/2)(q(x + y) − q(x) − q(y)) = x^T A y is symmetric and satisfies q(x) = b_q(x, x).
properties.why: The processes of polarization and evaluating on the diagonal (x, x) are mutual inverses over fields where 2 is invertible.

assumptions.assumption: The characteristic of the field K is different from 2 (char(K) ≠ 2).
assumptions.breaks_when: char(K) = 2, where 2 is not invertible in K, preventing division by 2 in symmetrizing matrices or recovering the form via polarization.

assumptions.assumption: The vector space V is finite-dimensional.
assumptions.breaks_when: V is infinite-dimensional, where finite coordinate vectors and finite n × n matrix representations are not directly defined.

failure_modes.signature: The polar form B'(x, y) = Q(x + y) − Q(x) − Q(y) satisfies B'(x, x) = 0 for all x (it is alternating), so Q(x) cannot be recovered as B'(x, x)/2.
failure_modes.cause: Division by 2 is undefined because 1 + 1 = 0 in characteristic 2.

failure_modes.signature: The kernel of the associated bilinear form contains non-zero vectors, or det(A) = 0.
failure_modes.cause: The coefficient matrix A has one or more zero eigenvalues, lowering the rank of the form.
